thread:
inc-bot: PAGING: p99 latency spike detected for /v1/stream (region: us-west-2). Alert: latency_slo_breach. p95 -> 340ms, p99 -> 2.1s, streaming stalls observed. @oncall rotation: @Ingrid (SRE) has been paged. :rotating_light:

oncall-bot: Acknowledge: Ingrid (SRE) is on call and will follow up. Incident channel opened. Runbook: /runbooks/streaming-latency.md

Ingrid (SRE): I'm on it. Initial glance at charts: sudden p99 jump at 12:37 UTC, concurrent connections up ~15%. Streaming stalls (clients waiting for token flush). Linking dashboard: https://dash.redwood-inference.internal/d/streaming-latency

Ashley (Platform): seeing correlated GPU ECC correctable errors on node gpu-node-31 starting 12:35 UTC. NVML reports increased correctables. Could cause kernel retries and stalls.

Raj (Infra): I'm pulling node telemetry. `ssh gpu-node-31 dmesg | tail -n 40` shows repeated PCIe link resets and `GPU ECC corrected` messages. Suspect flaky card or thermally-triggered microretries.

Ingrid (SRE): Good catch. For live mitigation, let's reduce traffic to that node and trigger routing fallback to cpu-quantized pool for streaming sessions that would otherwise land there. Ashley, can you push a quick routing policy change?

Ashley (Platform): Doing a soft-drain: updating routing policy `route: prefer=us-west-2:exclude_node=gpu-node-31 weight:cpu-quantized=1.0` will send new sessions away. Increasing canary weight to fallback model 100%. Applying now.

inc-bot: ACTION: routing policy updated by Ashley (Platform) at 12:42 UTC. New sessions are routed to fallback pool.

Olivia (Customer Success): Heads-up: Acme (enterprise) is on lower-latency SLA, they reported degraded streaming. I've told them we're investigating and routing around a problematic node; will follow up with ETA.

Ingrid (SRE): Starting graceful drain of active pods on gpu-node-31 to avoid kill storms. Command run: ```kubectl drain gpu-node-31 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60``` Watching connection handoffs.

Raj (Infra): While draining, NVML logs spiked with `gpuReset` events. I'm also seeing a thermal sensor climb but below hard throttle. Kernel: `NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus` once at 12:44. This points to hardware instability, schedule a quarantine.

Ingrid (SRE): Quarantine plan: cordon node, drain, add to quarantine pool for bake/test, then repro on maintenance. Already cordoned. Setting tag `quarantine:ecc-suspect` and removing from rotation.

Ashley (Platform): Quarantine tag applied and autoscaler will avoid the node. I've toggled `graceful-fallback` routing to stay on for 30m. Monitoring p99 and streaming stall count.

inc-bot: NOTE: customer impact flagged -> Acme: degraded streaming; number of affected requests estimated ~0.3% of total in us-west-2 during the spike window.

Olivia (Customer Success): Sent templated message to Acme: "We're routing around a hardware issue in one of our GPU nodes and will follow up with a postmortem. No data was exposed; sessions are continuing on fallback models."

Ingrid (SRE): Metrics after mitigation: p95 back to 120ms, p99 down to 420ms, streaming stall rate dropped ~95%. Still watching tail; ETA for full stabilization 15-30m while drains finish and autoscaler rebalances.

Raj (Infra): I'll raise a hardware ticket with the colo provider and schedule an out-of-band test. Serial console logs captured and attached to ticket. Suggest RMA for the GPU if we repro on maintenance.

Ashley (Platform): For immediate resiliency, I'm toggling a shorter KV-cache TTL and enabling more aggressive batching for fallback pool to keep cost/latency balanced. Pushing config: ```service.config.routing.fallback=true
service.config.cache.kv_ttl=30s
service.config/batching.max_batch_ms=12```

Ingrid (SRE): Documenting mitigation steps in the incident board and will own postmortem. Initial severity: Sev2 (partial SLO breach, isolated to us-west-2).

Olivia (Customer Success): I'll coordinate follow-up comms with Acme after the postmortem is ready.

Ingrid (SRE): Handoff: @Raj taking infra lead for hardware ticketing and RMA; @Ashley will own routing rollback once node is back in health; @Olivia will handle customer comms. I'll continue until the postmortem is published. Closing live mitigation phase; reopening if p99 > 700ms. :white_check_mark:

inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigation applied, node quarantined, customer notified. Next update requested in 60 minutes or on any regression.
